intro_html: This is meat-and-potatoes comfort food with a ranch twist, and it could not be simpler. Tender ranch pork over potatoes and carrots gives you 52 grams of protein a bowl for about $3.50 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings means one pot feeds you well for a whole week.
cost_closing_html: About $3.50 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Every serving runs about 551 calories with 52 grams of protein.
upsell_html: Simple, hearty, and cheap. Sometimes the plain-looking meals are the ones you crave most. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: One packet of ranch seasoning is all the flavor this needs. Skip the separate herbs and spices entirely.
Buy pork loin over tenderloin for this. At about $2 a pound it keeps the whole bowl easy on the budget.
Shredded carrots come pre-bagged and ready to go, which saves you the peeling and chopping when you are already cooking a big batch.
make_it: Rub the pork loin with a little olive oil and set it in the slow cooker.
Add the potatoes and shredded carrots around the pork.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix over everything and dot the top with butter.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Shred the pork and stir it through the buttery ranch juices.
Divide the pork, potatoes, and carrots into your containers.
